keyPlayers.name: Yaxel Lendeborg
keyPlayers.note: Lottery pick. Projected MOP (19/11/3 blocks in championship).

keyPlayers.name: Tre Johnson Jr.
keyPlayers.note: Part of tallest frontcourt in America.

keyPlayers.name: Mara (center)
keyPlayers.note: Historic height. Uncoverable on both ends.

strengths: #1 defense in America (scheme-proof). Tallest frontcourt in college basketball. Size compounds in tournament play. Two losses all year by combined 8 pts.
weaknesses: Point guard depth (Cadeau OUT). Limited ball-handling besides Lendeborg. Perimeter 3PT volume below elite teams.
narrative: Dusty May's defensive masterpiece. Size advantage grows exponentially in tournament. Elite defense + tallest roster = championship formula. Championship DNA: 1 seed with easiest path (Akron MAC team, ISU not focused on D, Houston neutral court).

keyPlayers.name: Cameron Boozer
keyPlayers.note: NPOY. Highest KenPom O rating in history.

keyPlayers.name: Caleb Foster
keyPlayers.note: OUT indefinitely. Second scoring option gone.

strengths: Boozer is historically transcendent scorer (22.7/10.2). Top-4 offense. Top-2 defense. Conference tournament momentum (ACC champ).
weaknesses: 7-man rotation fatigues by E8. Foster OUT = depth crisis. Boozer 37+ min/game unsustainable. Hardest path (UConn #9 KenPom + MSU Izzo expertise). No secondary scorer after Foster injury.
ourPick: Elite 8 (loses to UConn 72-71, UConn's 9-man rotation grinds Duke down)
narrative: Boozer is generational talent but can't carry thin rotation deep. Fatigue + injuries + UConn's depth = upset in E8. By game 5 (E8), rotation has played 80+ minutes on short rest.

keyPlayers.name: Jaden Bradley
keyPlayers.note: Big 12 POY. Defensive stopper. Makes 6 teammates better.

keyPlayers.name: Peat
keyPlayers.note: Interior presence. Back from injury = fresh.

strengths: 7 players average 8.7+ PPG (deepest roster). No injuries. Top-5 O, top-3 D. Only 2 losses all year. Won Big 12 in 3 games (freshest 1-seed). Safest, most balanced team.
weaknesses: No single transcendent scorer (if Bradley struggles, who takes final shot?). Depth can be unpredictable variance. One less day rest vs Michigan coming in.
ourPick: Runner-up (loses to Michigan 72-68 in championship game)
narrative: Safest 1-seed. Depth insulates vs variance. Self-correcting offense. Makes final Four as deepest team but Michigan's size advantage in championship too much.

strengths: Defending champs with experience. 5 double-figure scorers (depth). Chinyelu elite rebounding (11.7 RPG). #9 offense nationally. Won SEC tournament early (extra rest).
weaknesses: S16/E8 in Houston (structural disadvantage for them, Houston's home court). Haugh can be inconsistent (0-for games). Interior vulnerable to elite teams.
narrative: Defending champ curse. Early SEC exit leaves them rested but Houston's home court + Sampson's defensive architecture from 2025 title game rematch = Florida loses in own backyard intellectually.

keyPlayers.name: 9-man rotation
keyPlayers.note: Hurley's rotation advantage. 3 of last 4 title games.

strengths: Dan Hurley 3 of last 4 championship games (tournament DNA). 9-man rotation (deepest in field). 14-0 ATS in NCAA Tournament historically. Top-11 defense. Championship experience.
weaknesses: Recent losses to Creighton/Marquette show inconsistency. Gassed after Duke E8 war. Can't match Michigan's size in potential F4. Limited secondary scorers (Karaban only 12.9 PPG).
ourPick: Final Four (beats Duke 72-71 in E8 upset, loses to Arizona 75-70 in F4)
narrative: Hurley's tournament DNA + 9-man depth outlasts Duke's thin rotation. But Arizona depth edges UConn in F4 when UConn fatigued from Duke war.

keyPlayers.name: Caleb Smith
keyPlayers.note: NCAA assists record pursuit. One assist behind Hurley all-time.

strengths: #2 offense in KenPom (best besides Illinois #1). Smith/Loyer backcourt precision. 4 Big Ten tournament games shows offensive consistency.
weaknesses: Defense collapsed: went 6-7 down stretch, D dropped #20→#88. BEFORE 4 B10 tourney games = compounding fatigue. Can't defend at E8 level. Arizona's balance exposes one-dimensional approach.
ourPick: Sweet 16 (beats BYU 84-76, loses to Arizona 81-73 in E8)
narrative: Offensive firepower beats early opponents but defense can't hold vs Arizona's balance + elite D at E8. Late-season collapse before tournament = fatigue catching up.

strengths: Momcilovic 50% 3PT (unsolvable math problem). Top-10 defense. Lipsey elite PG play. Fresh (only 2 conf tourney games, 6 days rest).
weaknesses: 4-4 late-season slide shows offensive inconsistency. When ISU goes cold, they're beatable. One-dimensional offense (Momcilovic too predictable by S16).
ourPick: Elite 8 (beats Virginia 70-65 in S16, loses to Michigan 69-63 in E8)
narrative: Momcilovic's 50% 3PT beats Virginia's pace-heavy defense in S16, but Michigan's elite D (held Big Ten <30% 3PT) contains even Momcilovic in E8.

keyPlayers.name: Kingston Flemings
keyPlayers.note: Lottery pick. Best frosh Sampson coached. Shot-creator.

strengths: S16/E8 IN HOUSTON (home court = 3+ pts). Sampson HoF defensive architect. 62.9 PPG allowed (top-5 D). Sampson beat Florida in 2025 title game. Prep time advantage grows each round.
weaknesses: Offense KenPom #14 (mid-pack). May not have enough scoring for truly elite defenses. Sampson scheme relies on preparation time.
ourPick: Final Four (beats Florida 62-58 in E8 at Houston, loses to Michigan 68-61 in F4)
narrative: Houston's home court edge + Sampson's defensive mastery = Cinderella run. But Michigan's size neutralizes Sampson's scheme in F4 at neutral court.

strengths: 10-game winning streak. 3-peat MAC champions. All senior core (37%+ 3PT). 7 DAYS REST (maximum in field). Opponents (TTU + Holloway-less Bama) both imploding/fatigued.
weaknesses: MAC competition level. Will face elite defense in S16. Limited offensive diversity (3PT-dependent).
ourPick: Sweet 16 (beats TTU 79-74 in R32, beats Holloway-less Alabama 79-74 in R32, loses to Michigan 82-62 in S16)
narrative: Perfect storm Cinderella: 7 days rest + two injured opponents (Toppin ACL, Holloway arrested) = sweet 16 run. But hits Michigan's elite D wall in S16.

strengths: Dybantsa: 25.3 PPG (#1 nationally), 93 pts in 3 Big 12 tourney games, projected #1 pick. Highest individual ceiling in field (35+ PPG games possible).
weaknesses: DEFENSE 177th (worst in bracket). Saunders OUT (ACL) = D cratered. Can't win defensive games. Only weapon on team. By S16, defenses force ball from Dybantsa.
ourPick: Sweet 16 (beats Gonzaga (Huff OUT) 83-76 in R32, loses to Purdue 84-76 in S16)
narrative: Dybantsa's historic scoring (93 pts in 3 tourney games) carries past wounded Gonzaga, but Purdue #2 offense forces ball from his hands in S16.

strengths: Beat Michigan, Illinois, MSU, Purdue on road (4 tourney teams). Boyd Final Four experience. 3rd-fewest turnovers nationally. Fresh (only 2 conf tourney games, 6 days rest).
weaknesses: 62nd defense is vulnerability. Limited depth. Ceiling limited by defensive floor. Can't outscore elite offenses.
ourPick: Sweet 16 (beats Arkansas 75-71 in R32, loses to Arizona 78-72 in S16)
narrative: Wisconsin's elite wins (beat Mich/Ill/MSU/Purdue) + fresh legs (only 2 conf games) beat fatigued Arkansas in R32. But Arizona's balanced attack + elite D too much in S16.

strengths: 16-1 since Jan 10 (hottest team in field). A-10 tournament champs. Elite perimeter defense (57 steals, Lewis A-10 ROY). Wilson OUT for UNC = VCU's path opens.
weaknesses: Limited offensive firepower. Ceiling = elite D can't outscore better offenses. 70 PPG max games. Loses to Illinois #1 offense (offensive ceiling reached).
ourPick: Round of 32 (beats UNC 71-66 upset, loses to Illinois 82-71)
narrative: VCU upset of Wilson-less UNC makes noise, but Illinois #1 offense too much firepower for elite defense ceiling.

strengths: Only 7 KenPom spots from Kentucky (near parity). UK lost 5/7 games down stretch (fatigued). Quaintance doubtful (UK's best interior). Gavalyugov hot hand + 56.5% inside arc.
weaknesses: Can't sustain vs Iowa State's elite D (top-10). Offensive ceiling capped. Limited depth.
ourPick: Round of 32 (beats Kentucky 72-68 upset, loses to Iowa State 74-63)
narrative: Santa Clara upset of fatigued Kentucky validates Pope's defensive coaching, but Iowa State's top-10 D holds SC to 63 PPG ceiling.
